3.text: perform. He lifts his staff, and touches the competitors one by one. Half

6.text: Stars and Constellations. — Stars and constellations also belong to

7.text: the vaˊɪrg̣ɪt. The most important is the Polar Star, which is called in the

8.text: Chukchee language Iluˊkälin-eˊñer or Iluˊk-eˊñer (“motionless star”), or Äᵋlqeˊp-

9.text: eˊñer (“nail star”), or Unp-eˊñer (“the pole-stuck star”). This latter name

10.text: occurs throughout Asia. It suggests the existence of a simile in which all

11.text: other stars move around the Polar Star as horses or reindeer move around

12.text: a pole to which they are tethered. The house of the Polar Star stands in

13.text: the zenith. Directly under it is a hole through which it is possible to pass

14.text: from one world to another. Through a series of these holes the Polar Star

15.text: can be seen in all the lower and higher worlds, while the other constellations

16.text: change with the different worlds. Carrying this idea further, the house of

17.text: the Polar Star is supposed to be higher than that of any other star. It is

18.text: made of a material similar to ice,² and on the top of it is set the beacon-

20.text: Next in importance to the Polar Star are Arcturus and Vega, which are

21.text: called “Heads” (Leˊutti). Arcturus is called “Front Head” (Yanoʟaˊut), and

22.text: Vega is called “Rear Head” (Yaaʟaˊut). They are said to be brothers or

23.text: cousins. In the night-time, when travelling through the open tundra, the

24.text: Chukchee find their direction by comparing the position of both “Heads” to

25.text: each other and to the Polar Star. The “Front Head,” Arcturus, is often

26.text: called the “chief” or the “guide” of the stars.

27.text: The stars Altair and Tarared of the constellation Eagle are combined

28.text: by the Chukchee into a separate constellation, and are called Pehiˊttin. This

29.text: constellation is believed to usher in the light of the new year, because it

30.text: begins to appear above the horizon at the time of the winter solstice. The

31.text: Reindeer Chukchee and most of the families of the Maritime Chukchee sacri-

32.text: fice to Pehiˊttin at the time of his first appearance. I was told, both on the

33.text: Kolyma and the Anadyr, that Pehiˊttin was a forefather of the tribe, who,

34.text: after death, ascended to heaven; but I could not procure any further details.

35.text: Other stars and constellations known to the Chukchee are not considered

36.text: special vaˊɪrg̣ɪt. The principal ones are described below.

37.text: Orion, which is called Rulteˊnnin, is said to be an archer with a

38.text: crooked back. His name is derived from the same root as the adjective ni-

39.text: ruˊltᴀ-qin (“crooked”). Star λ of the constellation forms his head; α and γ,
